# OpenAI's Custom GPT Migration Won't Carry Actions to Plugins

Custom GPTs are scheduled to retire on December 11, 2026, and OpenAI's plugin migration does not move custom actions. Here is a 40-day runbook for finding, rebuilding and re-sharing the GPTs your teams depend on.

By Rajesh Beri·November 1, 2026·11 min read

Share:

Illustration generated using AI

If a custom GPT in your workspace calls an external API, the one-click migration will not keep that workflow running, and you have 40 days to rebuild it. Custom GPTs are scheduled to become inaccessible on December 11, 2026, according to Developers Digest's summary of OpenAI's retirement FAQ. OpenAI's migration guide says plainly that "custom actions do not transfer through the migration workflow." Instructions, knowledge files and connected apps do move. So the job this month is to find the GPTs with actions, decide which ones deserve a rebuild, and give your engineers enough lead time to do it.

A custom action is a connection that lets a GPT in ChatGPT call an outside API: the model picks the call, generates the JSON input from a schema you described, and the action executes it. A plugin is OpenAI's replacement package, which can hold skills (instructions for a task), apps (connections to other services), or both.

## What Moves to a Plugin and What Stays Behind

Text and files move, while integrations and access settings mostly do not. This table combines OpenAI's migration guide with Developers Digest's reading of the FAQ:

GPT feature | After migration | What you do 
---|---|---
Instructions | Become a skill | Test that the skill triggers; use an @ mention where it must run 
Knowledge files | Copied as reference files | Check that answers still cite the right material 
Connected apps | Stay in the plugin | Confirm each app is enabled and accounts have access 
Custom actions | Do not transfer | Rebuild on a supported app or a custom MCP server 
Selected model | Does not carry over; Enterprise defaults apply | Rerun familiar prompts and compare the output 
Sharing | Replacement starts private | Share again, then have a recipient install and test it 
Drafts | Only the latest published version moves | Publish needed edits first 

Migration also freezes the original. The GPT stays usable until retirement but turns read-only, and its creator cannot delete it. Past chats do not move to the plugin, per EdTech Innovation Hub. OpenAI's FAQ, as excerpted in search results on November 1, 2026, says existing conversations stay accessible after retirement with no action needed. The migration guide still tells you to save useful prompts and identify the context you need.

## The Dates, and Where the Sources Disagree

December 11 is the date to plan around, and OpenAI itself says it can move. The FAQ's wording, as quoted by Developers Digest, is that dates are "subject to change" and "a target date is not a guarantee." Virtualization Review adds that timing "can vary by account and workspace." OpenAI's Help Center returned a 403 to a scripted fetch on November 1, 2026, so the dates below come from write-ups that cite it, and the FedRAMP details come from its GPT help article as excerpted in search results that day. Check the live FAQ from a browser before you send a date to your organization.

Date | Milestone | Scope 
---|---|---
September 11, 2026 | Admin notice | Enterprise 
October 26, 2026 | New custom GPT creation ended; unmigrated GPTs stay editable | Affected Enterprise workspaces except FedRAMP, per Developers Digest, Virtualization Review and OpenAI's help article 
December 11, 2026 | Standard retirement | All plans 
February 11, 2027 | Retirement for FedRAMP workspaces and workspaces with an approved deferral | Some Enterprise 

Two gaps remain. iTechnically Kan lists the October 26 cutoff without limiting it to Enterprise. The FAQ excerpts from that day say personal accounts (Free, Go, Plus and Pro) cannot create or publish new GPTs, and they send Business workspaces to their workspace notice and settings, so Business owners should check there. And neither Virtualization Review nor EdTech Innovation Hub explains what qualifies for a deferral or how to request one. Ask your OpenAI account team in writing, and keep planning for December 11 until you hold an approval. The same excerpts say a deferral alone does not preserve the ability to create new GPTs. FedRAMP workspaces are listed for February 11 and can still create GPTs, so confirm that date with the same team.

## Why Custom Actions Are the Expensive Part

A rebuilt action is a second plugin with its own permissions, hosting and testing. OpenAI's rebuild guide has you ask the original GPT for a rebuild prompt, check that prompt against your saved action settings, and create a new Sites plugin, where Sites hosts the MCP server. The result is separate from the migrated plugin, and you can use both in one conversation. Sites plugins do not currently support editing skills or reference files. Plan on one old GPT becoming two things to own.

The permissions catch is the part most likely to surprise an admin. The migration guide says built-in migration does not need Upload plugins or Upload plugins with custom MCP servers. The rebuild guide says the Site owner publishing an MCP-backed plugin needs Upload plugins and Create plugins with MCPs, both off by default in Enterprise. So a workspace can finish migration prep and still block every MCP rebuild. The two pages also name that second permission differently, so check the label in your own admin console.

Access changes as well. Teammates need at least viewer access to the plugin, its app and the Site, and each person "installs and connects with their own account." If your old action ran on one shared service credential, compare the two models with your security lead, because per-user sign-in can change who reaches which records.

The case for the rebuild is real. OpenAI's MCP guidance tells builders to "enforce authorization in the MCP server for every request; never rely on the model to decide whether a user has access," and to setreadOnlyHint and destructiveHint to match what each tool does. The same plugin package and public directory serve ChatGPT and Codex. An action that sat inside one GPT becomes a server with an owner, which your security team can review once and which other plugins can reuse. For the controls around that server, see our MCP server governance guide, and test the tool design: a generic MCP connector lost to no tools at all in UNICEF's benchmark.

## How to Host the Rebuild When the API Is Private

Your hosting choice comes down to where the API lives. The default in OpenAI's rebuild guide is a Sites plugin that reuses your existing API where possible, and the server still needs an approved connection to that API. For another host, you follow OpenAI's Build an MCP server guide, which calls for a streamable HTTP endpoint and OAuth 2.1 for user login.

For systems behind your firewall, Secure MCP Tunnel connects private servers without inbound firewall rules: a customer-runtunnel-client polls OpenAI for queued requests and forwards them. It needs outbound HTTPS to api.openai.com:443 and does not support public plugin distribution. Two details deserve a test before you commit. A tunnel tied only to a personal Platform organization "doesn't automatically appear in an Enterprise/Edu workspace," and tunnel permissions sit at the Platform organization level while ChatGPT access is governed by workspace permissions. The page does not describe a general workspace rollout, so prove it with one real teammate account first.

Auth secrets stay out of the package. Plugin manifests declare connection settings, not credentials, and the rebuild guide says to leave credentials out of the prompt you hand to Plugin Creator.

## What Migration Costs

Conversion is free, and the running costs depend on your pricing model. OpenAI's guide says converting a GPT to a plugin does not consume credits, while editing or updating one does under credit-based pricing. It adds that Instant Chat is "generally unlimited" under that pricing but a request can switch to a reasoning model, and that Work consumes credits based on model and tokens. iTechnically Kan cites the FAQ as saying that, in Enterprise workspaces, a migrated GPT without apps in Instant Chat has no incremental cost.

So a simple prompt GPT may cost nothing more, while a workflow that routes through Work now draws on your credit pool. OpenAI also notes that a zero overage limit prevents spending beyond the shared allocation. Run your top five replacements for a week and read the usage before you roll them out. Our earlier piece on ChatGPT Enterprise spend controls covers the admin side.

## This Is the Second Time OpenAI Has Done This

ChatGPT builders have been through a forced move before, and GPTs were the official replacement then. When OpenAI wound down the original plugins beta, Zapier told customers that new conversations would end on March 19, 2024 and existing ones would stop working on April 9, 2024. Zapier now points those users to Zapier MCP.

Google is running a similar change on a slower clock with a kinder default. Its admin guide says Business and Enterprise users lose Gems no sooner than March 1, 2027, and that Drive permissions and sharing settings carry over to the converted skills, which arrive as inactive drafts. Gems used in Workspace apps have to be recreated by hand. Our Gems coverage has the details. Skills are also moving toward a shared format: Codex and GitHub Copilot read Anthropic's Agent Skills, which makes instructions the most portable thing you own here.

A correction to our own record: our April story on Workspace Agents replacing custom GPTs carried a May 15 date. Current reporting puts the retirement at December 11.

# GPT Plus用户天塌了！OpenAI官宣，Codex和ChatGPT共享额度。

GPT Plus用户这两天是真的被按在地上摩擦了三回。

前天Pro订阅费直接全额返成API额度，Plus用户连汤都没喝到。昨天Codex额度翻倍，又没Plus的事。

有人开玩笑，说Plus用户存在的意义，大概就是给Pro当个额度计算的当量单位。100刀等于10 plus，200刀等于20 plus，纯纯的背景板。

今天第三刀来了——Codex和ChatGPT要共享额度了，这次Plus终于“有份”了。好事永远轮不到你，吃亏的时候倒是一个不落。

说实话，刷到这消息的第一反应就是：完了，那些又写代码又重度用ChatGPT的人要哭了。

OpenAI又一次颠覆了我的认知。以前Codex和普通ChatGPT多少还能算“各吃各的”，现在直接把额度池到一起，变成一个总池子。而且是按token计费的那种精细计量，模型越强、任务越复杂，烧得越快。

很多人同时开着这两个工具，为什么？因为Codex写代码、重构、跑任务确实好用，ChatGPT日常问答、写文档、做研究也离不开。可正因为两边都重度使用，这个共享额度一出来，就成了“双开党”的噩梦。

之前我写过一篇《告别焦虑，一文掌握 GPT 额度》。现在，天塌了——额度要开始抢着用了。

### 消息一出，网友炸了锅

这消息一发布，评论区直接热闹了，各种观点都有。

有人直接开怼，说OpenAI这是“羊毛剪到家了”——“Plus的20刀本来就紧，现在还要和Codex抢，还不如直接买Pro”。

也有技术流的网友看得很透彻。反正有技术，可以把ChatGPT想办法搞给codex用。

有网友甚至脑补以下场景：

还有一条生路

好消息是Instant及时聊天被排除在外，坏消息是Instant聊天默认使用低端模型且不带思考模式，比如GPT 5.6 Terra

不过复杂任务、长上下文、agent模式，就全算进总池子。

还有网友觉得，这迟早会变成行业常态——Anthropic那边Claude Code和普通Claude也在收紧。 Google gemini估计也快了。 以后订阅制AI不再是“无限畅聊”，而是“有限额度池，按使用强度分配”。

### 到底发生了什么

OpenAI官方在Help Center更新了说明：从12月起，Plus、Pro和Business计划的使用额度将在ChatGPT和Codex之间共享。这是因为他们要把Work的agent能力正式整合进主ChatGPT体验里。

计量方式改为token制：模型越强、任务越复杂、上下文越长，消耗越快。Instant聊天不计入这个共享额度。用户可以在Settings > Usage里看到合并后的剩余额度和重置时间。

额度用完后，可以等重置、升级计划，或者直接买credits继续用。

范围：Plus、Pro、Business（具体日期还没精确到哪一天，但方向已经明确）。

### 为什么要搞这个

原因很简单：算力成本和产品统一。

Codex和ChatGPT Work本来就有共享倾向，现在把普通ChatGPT的重度使用也拉进来，能更精准地管理算力。同时把agent能力深度整合进主产品，用户体验上更统一，但代价就是额度不再“分家”。

### 最后说一句

根据OpenAI的尿性，用户反对，他就会退让。最好的结局就是额度统一，但是额度Double。也就是说，实际的额度比新政策之前更多。

12 月之后，你会先把额度留给写代码，还是留给聊天问问题？评论区说说看。

# OpenAI API Credits: ChatGPT Pro and Business Now Include Up to $500 a Month

As of October 28, 2026, ChatGPT Pro comes with monthly OpenAI API credits equal to the plan price: $100, $200 or $500. ChatGPT Business gets $20 per Standard seat and $100 per Premium seat, pooled up to $500 a month. Plus doesn't qualify. You claim it once, it renews automatically, and whatever you don't use in the month is gone.

This almost slipped past me because the prices didn't change. It's a line in OpenAI's release notes. It also matches a deal Anthropic launched three weeks earlier nearly dollar for dollar, which tells you what these two are competing for: the people building on them, not only the people chatting with them.

## Who gets OpenAI API credits, and how much?

Plan | Monthly API credit 
---|---
ChatGPT Pro 100 | $100 
ChatGPT Pro 200 | $200 
ChatGPT Pro 500 | $500 
Business Standard seat | $20 per paid seat, pooled 
Business Premium seat | $100 per paid seat, pooled 
Business workspace cap | $500 total a month 
Plus, free trials | Not eligible 
Enterprise, Edu, legacy Codex seats | Not listed as eligible 

Your subscription has to be active for at least 7 days first, and the first grant is prorated. The full rate card these credits spend against is on my OpenAI API pricing page.

## Where the Business cap kicks in

The pool is the smaller of ($20 × Standard seats + $100 × Premium seats) and $500. So the cap arrives faster than you'd think.

Workspace | Before the cap | You get | Per seat 
---|---|---|---
2 Standard | $40 | $40 | $20 
10 Standard | $200 | $200 | $20 
25 Standard | $500 | $500 | $20 
50 Standard | $1,000 | $500 | $10 
10 Standard + 4 Premium | $600 | $500 | $35.71 

Annual workspaces get the full year up front, capped at $6,000, and it expires when the billing cycle ends.

## What does the credit actually buy?

These are my own worked examples on OpenAI's standard rates, read November 1: GPT-6.1 Sol at $2 in and $10 out per million tokens, and GPT-6 Luna at $0.10 and $0.50. The token counts are assumptions, so swap in yours.

Job | Tokens in / out | Model | Cost each | $20 buys | $100 buys 
---|---|---|---|---|---
Sort one inbound email | 2,000 / 300 | Luna | $0.00035 | 57,142 | 285,714 
Summarize a long document | 20,000 / 1,500 | Sol | $0.055 | 363 | 1,818 
One agent run | 30,000 / 3,000 | Sol | $0.09 | 222 | 1,111 

For a small business, that's the real point. A 10-seat Business workspace gets $200 a month, which is enough to run an email-sorting or document-summary automation for free. You've probably been paying for that seat either way. If you want one of those built properly, that's the AI implementation work I do.

## How do you claim it?

- Use the same email for your ChatGPT account and API account.
- On Pro, open Settings > Billing in ChatGPT. On Business, open the workspace billing settings or the Admin Console.
- Find the API credits benefit, pick the API organization, and confirm.
- Check the balance in API Platform billing settings.

You don't need to add a payment method to use the grant. On Business, one person must own both the ChatGPT workspace and the API organization. An admin role isn't enough, which will trip up plenty of small companies where the person who set up ChatGPT isn't the person who set up the API.

## The catches

- No rollover. Monthly grants expire at the end of the billing cycle.
- It isn't ChatGPT credits. ChatGPT credits buy more usage inside ChatGPT. These don't raise your ChatGPT or signed-in Codex limits at all.
- No Codex through API keys. OpenAI excludes it by name.
- One link. One subscription or workspace links to one API organization, and an organization can hold only one active link.
- Teammates get nothing automatically. A ChatGPT seat doesn't give anyone API access.
- Rate limits still apply. Credits aren't a higher tier.
- It can go away. OpenAI says the benefit "may change or be removed in the future."

## OpenAI vs Claude API credits

OpenAI | Anthropic 
---|---
$100 plan | Pro 100: $100 | Max: $100 
$200 plan | Pro 200: $200 | Ultra: $200 
$500 plan | Pro 500: $500 | None sold 
Team seats | $20 Standard, $100 Premium | $20 Standard, $100 Premium 
Team cap | $500 a month | $500 a month 
$20 plan | Plus: none | Pro: none 

They're the same deal at every rung they share. If you pay for one already, you don't need to switch for this. I covered Anthropic's side, including what it excludes, on my Claude API credits page.

## Should you upgrade for the credit?

Only if you'd spend it. If you already pay OpenAI $100 a month in API bills, Pro 100 now pays for itself, and the ChatGPT plan is effectively free. If you have no API project, a credit you never touch is worth $0, and it shouldn't change my read on whether ChatGPT Pro is worth it.

## Frequently Asked Questions

- Does ChatGPT Pro include API credits?
- Yes, as of late October 2026. Pro subscribers can claim monthly OpenAI API credits equal to their plan price: $100 on Pro 100, $200 on Pro 200 and $500 on Pro 500. You have to claim it once and link an API organization, and your subscription must have been active for at least 7 days.
- Does ChatGPT Plus include API credits?
- No. OpenAI says Plus and free trials do not qualify. Eligible plans are Pro 100, Pro 200, Pro 500 and eligible Business workspaces with paid Standard or Premium seats. Enterprise, Edu and legacy Codex seats are not listed as eligible.
- How much in API credits does ChatGPT Business get?
- $20 per paid Standard seat plus $100 per paid Premium seat, pooled for the workspace and capped at $500 a month. The cap arrives at 25 Standard seats or 5 Premium seats. Workspaces billed annually upfront get a full-year grant at once, capped at $6,000.
- Do OpenAI API credits roll over?
- No. Monthly grants expire at the end of the subscription billing cycle, and unused credits do not roll over. Your first grant is also prorated for the time left in the billing period, so the first month may be smaller than the full amount.
- Are API credits the same as ChatGPT credits?
- No. ChatGPT usage credits extend what you can do inside ChatGPT and Codex when you sign in. API credits pay for apps and agents you build on the OpenAI API. OpenAI says these API credits do not raise your ChatGPT or signed-in Codex limits, and they do not cover Codex through API keys.

# Google DeepMind Unveils Genie 4 Real-Time World Model With Native Audio

Google DeepMind has announced Genie 4, an experimental AI model designed to generate and run interactive worlds in real time. The system produces more than a conventional video: people can move through a generated environment, change what happens with natural-language instructions and hear audio produced as the simulation develops.

The announcement, published on October 27, says Genie 4 combines capabilities from Google’s Gemini model family with a world simulator. Gemini Omni is used to help anchor the appearance and behavior of scenes, while other Gemini models provide reasoning intended to preserve continuity as the world changes.

## Scenes can be changed with natural language

A user can steer an active simulation by asking it to move the camera, change the weather or introduce a person or object. Google DeepMind says Gemini adapts those instructions to the surrounding scene and can continue guiding events between user inputs. The model is therefore intended to generate a world frame by frame and respond as the user interacts, rather than render a fixed clip from beginning to end.

The company also highlights more realistic movement and physical behavior, including scenarios involving collisions and aerodynamics. Its demonstrations include characters that move and respond to their environment, as well as simulations of multi-step tasks. In one example described by DeepMind, Gemini 4 Argon and Genie 4 simulate Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid playing checkers without using a physical robot.

## Audio is generated inside the simulation

Genie 4 is presented as Google DeepMind’s first real-time world model to generate audio natively. Its simulated environments can include ambient sounds such as wind or waves, along with music and interactive dialogue. Characters can converse and react to user inputs or events, according to the company.

That capability broadens the model’s potential uses beyond visual game-like environments. Google DeepMind says trusted testers are exploring applications in creative work, journalism, education, gaming and engineering, including scene pre-visualisation, interactive prototypes and simulation-based workflows. The company also describes world models as potentially useful for creating safer training environments for robots and AI agents. Those are stated research directions, not announced commercial products.

## Early access comes with limitations

Genie 4 is not broadly available. Google DeepMind has begun a research preview with a limited group of trusted testers. It says access is planned for Google AI Ultra subscribers through Project Genie and for early-access partners using the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

The model remains experimental. DeepMind says visual details and object permanence can drift during longer sessions, after several complex prompt changes or while navigating a scene. Complex physical interactions, accurate real-time audio, legible text, spatial accuracy and long-term consistency remain active research problems. The Decoder independently reported the same restricted rollout and described the model as limited in longer sessions and complex physics.

Google DeepMind says Genie 4-generated video and audio will carry SynthID, its imperceptible watermarking technology for identifying AI-generated content. For now, the release is best understood as a controlled research preview showing how language reasoning, visual simulation and sound might operate together in an interactive environment.

# Meta Model API

The Meta Model API (public preview) serves Meta Superintelligence Labs' Muse Spark models through an OpenAI-compatible API. The Meta provider extends the OpenAI provider and supports its compatible options.

note

This provider uses the Meta Model API atapi.meta.ai for Muse models. Meta retired the separate Llama API at api.llama.com on July 6, 2026.

## Setup

- Create an API key from the API keys tab on the Meta Model API dashboard.
- Set theMODEL_API_KEY environment variable, or specify apiKey or a custom apiKeyEnvar in your config.

providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3

meta:<model> defaults to the Responses API — Meta's full-feature surface and the one its docs recommend. Use meta:chat:<model> for the OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint, or meta:messages:<model> for the Anthropic-compatible Messages API. If you omit the model, the provider defaults to muse-spark-1.1; select muse-spark-1.3 explicitly to use the latest model.

## Available Models

Check the models page for the live list. As of writing:

- muse-spark-1.3 — latest model for coding and agentic workflows, with a 1,048,576-token context window, text/image/video/PDF input, tool calling, structured output, and search grounding.
- muse-spark-1.3-contributor — the same model with discounted pricing. Selecting this ID permits Meta to use your prompts and completions to train future models.
- muse-spark-1.1 — original Muse Spark model, still supported.

Both 1.3 IDs work with the Responses, Chat Completions, and Messages APIs. Meta notes that audio understanding in 1.3 is not fully supported and may produce degraded responses.

## Configuration
providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      reasoning_effort: high
      max_completion_tokens: 8192
      temperature: 1.0

### Configuration Options

The provider accepts compatible OpenAI provider options. Notable behavior:

- reasoning_effort — minimal, low, medium, high, or xhigh. When omitted, the model picks its own reasoning depth. Muse Spark does not support none; the provider rejects it with a clear error. Reasoning tokens bill at the output rate and count toward the output cap.
- max_completion_tokens — caps generation on the chat endpoint (Meta accepts max_tokens only as a deprecated alias; if you set it, the provider forwards it as the canonical max_completion_tokens). On the Responses API the cap is max_output_tokens, and the provider maps max_completion_tokens/max_tokens onto it. When unset, no cap is sent so reasoning can use the full output budget.
- temperature — supported (0–2, API default 1.0). Promptfoo sends its deterministic default of 0 unless you override it.
- response_format — structured output with guaranteed JSON schema matching.
- tools / tool_choice — parallel tool calling with streamed arguments.
- prompt_cache_retention — in_memory or 24h for prompt caching; cached prompt tokens bill at the cached-input rate.
- seed — best-effort determinism.

On Chat Completions and Responses, promptfoo rejectslogprobs, n > 1, stop, and logit_bias before sending a request. It also rejects stream because these integrations expect a complete JSON response. OpenAI-scoped environment defaults (OPENAI_TEMPERATURE, OPENAI_TOP_P, OPENAI_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS, penalty variables) are not applied to Meta requests.

### Cost Tracking

Promptfoo computes token cost from Meta's published pricing, including the discounted rate for cached input:

Model | Input / 1M | Cached input / 1M | Output / 1M 
---|---|---|---
muse-spark-1.3, muse-spark-1.1 | $1.25 | $0.15 | $4.25 
muse-spark-1.3-contributor | $0.10 | $0.002 | $0.20 

Contributor pricing requires opting into Meta's training data terms by selecting the Contributor model ID. Override token prices withcost, inputCost, outputCost, or cacheReadCost (USD per token) for custom rates. Token cost excludes web-search charges.

## Responses API

meta:<model> (the default) and meta:responses:<model> target Meta's /v1/responses endpoint — the only Meta endpoint that carries reasoning across turns, with built-in web-search grounding:
providers:
  - id: meta:responses:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      reasoning_effort: medium
      tools:
        - type: web_search

Withweb_search, the model grounds answers in real-time web results with inline citations. Web search bills separately ($2.50 per 1,000 queries) and is not included in promptfoo's computed token cost.

## Messages API

meta:messages:<model> targets Meta's Anthropic-compatible Messages endpoint (https://api.meta.ai/v1/messages) — the surface Anthropic-format coding agents such as Claude Code use. Use it to evaluate Muse Spark over the same wire format those agents send:
providers:
  - id: meta:messages:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      max_tokens: 8192

The provider extends the Anthropic provider, so its options (max_tokens, tools, image and document content blocks, etc.) apply. It defaults max_tokens to 131,072 and enables streaming so the Anthropic SDK can safely handle long generations; streamed output is aggregated before grading. Authentication uses your Meta key as a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer), matching Meta's docs — Anthropic-scoped settings like ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS, ANTHROPIC_TEMPERATURE, custom headers, and Claude Code OAuth credentials are deliberately ignored on this surface.

Muse Spark's reasoning arrives on this surface as encryptedredacted_thinking blocks, so the provider defaults showThinking to false to keep the ciphertext out of graded output.

## Using with coding-agent providers

Meta positions Muse Spark as a backend for coding agents, and promptfoo's agentic providers can evaluate those setups end to end. In both recipes, setapiKey explicitly: the agent subprocesses inherit your shell environment, and an explicit key guarantees your Meta key is used instead of an ambient OPENAI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY that belongs to another service.

### Codex CLI

Theopenai:codex-sdk provider drives Muse Spark over the Responses API:
providers:
  - id: openai:codex-sdk
    config:
      base_url: https://api.meta.ai/v1
      model: muse-spark-1.3
      apiKey: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'

The explicitapiKey is required — the provider does not read MODEL_API_KEY on its own, and without it an ambient OPENAI_API_KEY would be sent to the Meta endpoint instead.

### Claude Code

Theanthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider forwards config.env to the agent subprocess. Pass the environment Meta's guide prescribes, with apiKey set to your Meta key:
providers:
  - id: anthropic:claude-agent-sdk
    # Provider-level `env` outranks the eval's top-level `env`, pinning the
    # routing values a suite-wide ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (e.g. an Anthropic
    # gateway) would otherwise override — which would send the Meta key there.
    env:
      ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://api.meta.ai
      ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: ''
    config:
      apiKey: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://api.meta.ai
        ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'
        ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: ''
        ANTHROPIC_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH: 'true' # Claude Code disables MCP tool search for non-first-party hosts

warning

Do not omitapiKey, the empty ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS override, or the provider-level env block. The provider forwards its resolved API key into the agent subprocess as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY after env: is applied — if apiKey is unset and a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is exported in your shell, that Anthropic credential would be transmitted to Meta's endpoint. Clearing ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS prevents an inherited gateway or proxy secret from being sent to Meta. The provider-level env block matters because the subprocess environment is layered process.env < config.env < provider/suite env: without the pin, a top-level env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in the same config would silently re-route the agent — and your Meta key — to that URL.

Pin every model alias as shown — Claude Code otherwise routes background tasks, Plan Mode, or subagents to Claude models the Meta API doesn't serve. See Meta's coding agents guide for the full setup pattern.

## Example Usage
providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3
  - id: openai:gpt-5.5

prompts:
  - 'Summarize the following in one sentence: {{text}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      text: 'Promptfoo is an open-source tool for testing and evaluating LLM apps.'

Get started with a runnable example:
npx promptfoo@latest init --example provider-meta

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.meta.ai/v1 (override with apiBaseUrl; the Messages surface uses the bare host https://api.meta.ai).
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions (/chat/completions) and Responses (/responses) endpoints, plus the Anthropic-compatible Messages (/messages) endpoint.
- Rate limits apply per team, not per key: 3,000 RPM / 4M TPM for Standard models and 100 RPM / 3M TPM for Contributor models.
- Full API documentation.

Meta.content:
# 缪斯奇想：Meta重返人工智能前沿

作者: aeks | 发布时间: 2026-11-01 00:07 | 更新时间: 2026-11-01 00:07

Meta表示，其Muse Wonder系列（包括Muse Wonder Full）具备前沿能力，意味着它属于目前全球性能最强的AI模型之一。公司在今天发布的博客文章中说，这些模型共同标志着Meta在能力扩展阶梯上的下一步，也是迈向“个人超级智能”的一次重大飞跃。

Muse Wonder系列模型将通过API以及Muse Code提供。Muse Code是一款借助AI编写软件的工具。Meta称，该系列最强版本将用于支撑其平台上的多种功能，其中包括Muse个人智能体。

扎克伯格去年大幅调整公司AI研究：他向新成立的Meta超级智能实验室投入数十亿美元，并聘请前Scale AI首席执行官Alexandr Wang领导该实验室。不过，这一过程并非一帆风顺，有些研究人员未能长期留在团队中。

Meta曾是AI领域的先行者。其Llama系列模型是大型实验室首批前沿开放权重模型之一，可下载并在个人硬件上运行，因此受到研究者和初创公司广泛采用。

但后来，由于连续几版模型表现不及预期，同时Anthropic、OpenAI和Google迅速推出更强模型，Meta一度落后。

今年4月，Meta公布了新实验室的首个模型Muse Spark。公司还发布了一个小型开放权重模型Muse Glimmer，并表示未来计划发布更大的开放权重模型。对于新的Muse Wonder模型是如何构建和训练的，Meta没有披露细节。

Meta称，Muse Wonder的目标是与最顶尖模型竞争。根据广泛使用的模型能力综合评分Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index，Muse Wonder最大版本超过Anthropic的第二强模型Claude Fable 5.1，仅次于Anthropic最强模型Claude Opus 5.5。

在部分专门基准测试中，Meta称该模型超过OpenAI最强模型GPT-6 Astra，也超过Claude Fable 5.1和Claude Opus 5.5，尤其在处理法律文档和开发软件方面表现更好。尽管基准测试并不总能准确反映现实表现，但对Meta的模型来说，这仍然是明显进步。

Muse Wonder还加入两项新功能，名为Active Memory（主动记忆）和Active Focus（主动聚焦），旨在让AI智能体更有效、更不容易失控。它们希望让模型持续锁定既定目标，避免在复杂任务中变得混乱。比如，在深度研究或大型软件项目中，这种能力可以减少代价高昂的错误和连锁错误。

Meta称，团队投入大量工作训练Muse Wonder拒绝生成危险内容，例如制造生物武器的配方或提供黑客帮助，并表示在衡量模型抵抗此类诱导能力的测试中表现较好。

不过，近期Anthropic、OpenAI及其他机构都出现过AI智能体失控事件，说明强大的AI模型在接到开放式指令时也可能偏离目标。Meta没有说明，在测试中由Muse Wonder驱动的智能体是否出现过类似失范行为，也没有披露针对该问题的具体应对措施。

扎克伯格上月在X上表示，公司推迟Muse系列发布，是为了进一步完善安全性。本月初，Meta还在博客文章中公布了一套框架，以确保在扩展模型能力时保持安全。

文章最后指出，Muse Wonder可能让本就激烈的AI竞赛进一步升温，也表明在风险不断上升的AI竞赛中，Meta正在重新具备竞争力。

Meta.content:
← IP News

# Meta’s AI Training Copyright Trial Set for 3 May 2027 – and the Works List Isn’t Final

A joint case management statement filed on 27 October 2026 in the Northern District of California puts Meta and Entrepreneur Media on trial on 3 May 2027, with four more publisher and author cases queued behind it. The fight is no longer about whether training on books is fair use - it is about how the books were acquired, and the works list is still being assembled out of Meta's own discovery responses.

The five copyright actions against Meta over its use of pirated books to train the Llama models now have a trial date. In a Joint Case Management Statement filed on 27 October 2026 in the Northern District of California (Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc., No. 3:23-cv-03417-VC, Dkt. No. 879), the parties record that, under the court’s 14 October 2026 order, Meta and Entrepreneur Media will prepare for trial on 3 May 2027 before Judge Vince Chhabria. The statement was filed under Civil Local Rule 16-9(a) ahead of a case management conference on 29 October 2026, and covers five captions being managed together: the Kadrey authors’ case, Entrepreneur Media (3:25-cv-09579), and the three publisher matters the parties call the “Three C’s” — Cambronne (3:26-cv-03725), Chicken Soup for the Soul (3:26-cv-02333) and Cognella (3:26-cv-04053).

The parties also propose what happens if the lead case settles: the 3 May slot passes down in order of filing, so Cambronne would go first, then Chicken Soup, then Cognella. One scheduling wrinkle remains in the statement — the pretrial conference set for 20 April 2027 collides with a Delaware Superior Court jury trial for Meta’s lead trial counsel (Conduent State Healthcare, LLC v. AIG Specialty Insurance Company, No. N18C-12-074), and Meta suggests moving the conference to 26 or 27 April while keeping the pretrial submission deadlines keyed to the original date.

The substantive dispute recorded in the statement is about acquisition, not training. Plaintiffs report that on the Friday before filing, former Meta employee Stephen Roller testified at deposition that he torrented and knowingly distributed Books3 — a dataset of some 196,000 pirated books — during the period he worked at Meta (2017 to 2023), and that he deleted his copy about a year ago, “[d]ue to all this litigation.” They note that as recently as Meta’s 24 August 2026 interrogatory responses, Meta had said it did not believe it obtained Books3 via BitTorrent or any other peer-to-peer protocol. Meta’s half of the statement disputes the characterisation squarely: it says Roller did not know when he downloaded the dataset, never testified that the download was for or at Meta rather than for himself or another employer, said he did not know whether more than one copy was downloaded, and did not confirm that the two colleagues plaintiffs name had copies of their own. The deleted copy, Meta adds, sat on Roller’s personal computer and was removed more than two years after he left the company. As TorrentFreak reports, Meta acknowledged in early 2024 that it used portions of Books3 to train Llama 1 and Llama 2 without saying how it obtained the dataset.

## What it changes

The useful part of this filing is not the gossip about a book club. It is a set of dates and procedural rulings that tell you, concretely, how an AI-training copyright case is actually won or lost — and almost none of it turns on the merits of fair use.

### Your list of asserted works is built out of the defendant’s discovery, not your own records

Entrepreneur Media must file an amended complaint by 6 November 2026, and the statement says it is expected to add more than 400 additional books and more than 140 additional magazine issues. Those works were not found in Entrepreneur’s own archive. They were identified in Meta’s interrogatory responses and search results served between 4 August and 30 September 2026, and in the 2 October 2026 opening report of plaintiffs’ torrenting expert, Dr David Choffnes, which plaintiffs say identifies more than 400 Entrepreneur books inside the shadow-library collections Meta torrented. Entrepreneur’s own position is blunt: only Meta knows which works it acquired and trained on, so the final list depends on Meta’s disclosures.

Read that as a planning rule. If your works may be in a training corpus, the complaint you file first is a placeholder. The real claim emerges from the defendant’s interrogatory responses and its expert’s corpus analysis, twelve to thirty months later, and the amendment window to capture it is measured in weeks. Build the litigation plan around a late conforming amendment rather than around the works you can name on day one.

### Registration and chain of title are the gating items — and the price of registration is about to move

Meta’s response to the proposed amendment is not a merits argument. It asks the court to order Entrepreneur and the Three C’s to hand over the proposed amended complaints, the lists of asserted works, all materials establishing their right to assert each work, and copies of copyright registrations for every proposed asserted work. Entrepreneur states it has already produced all author and writer agreements in its possession, with registration certificates possibly still to come.

That is the whole claim reduced to a paperwork exercise. A US infringement claim cannot be asserted on an unregistered US work, and every added title has to arrive with a registration and a clean chain from author to claimant. For publishers, agencies and in-house teams, the practical consequence is that the back catalogue has to be registration-complete and contract-complete before the corpus list lands, not after — which is where disciplined IP contract and rights-record management stops being administrative hygiene and starts being the difference between a 400-work claim and a 40-work one. There is also a cost clock: the Register of Copyrights submitted a new fee schedule to Congress on 14 July 2026 under 17 U.S.C. §708(b), which can take effect as early as 12 November 2026. If a bulk catch-up registration programme is on your list, the arithmetic changes this month.

### Timeliness, not relevance, is killing the best evidence

Plaintiffs want Meta ordered to produce documents hyperlinked inside documents it already produced, including a Google Drive folder titled “ML Books” and records of a Meta book club that may have used shadow-library books. Their legal theory is sound and they cite Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts v. Goldsmith, 598 U.S. 508, 533 (2023) for it: fair use is assessed separately for each use, so books taken from a shadow library and then read for pleasure are a second, unexcused use that sits outside any training-related defence.

Meta’s answer is a calendar. The two documents containing those links were produced on 17 August 2026; plaintiffs first asked for the linked files on 9 October 2026, which Meta says is more than a month after fact discovery closed and over three weeks after the Local Rule 37-3 deadline to raise discovery disputes. On that reasoning the folder never gets produced, whatever is in it. The same timeliness objection is aimed at the request for Meta’s torrenting expert’s prior reports from other BitTorrent matters, where Meta points out that Judge Hixson already denied an equivalent request directed at third-party OpenAI and that no objection was filed, making the ruling final.

The lesson generalises well beyond AI. Hyperlinked attachments, shared-drive folders and chat threads are now where the decisive admissions live, and they are not captured by ordinary document review — you have to notice the link, ask for the target, and ask while the discovery window is open. Diarise the dispute-raising deadline, not just the discovery cut-off.

### Provenance logs and personal devices are the real exposure for anyone training a model

The command-history fight is the most transferable part of the record. Back in March 2025 the court adopted a limited-discovery proposal that expressly defined “Documents” to include command-line history logs, naming the.bash_history file in the user home directories of servers used to download data. Plaintiffs say Meta produced none from the servers used during its torrenting periods until one surfaced in search-term results, that Judge Hixson then ordered full compliance — Meta dates that order to 11 September 2026 — and that they now want the court to order Meta to state whether any such files were deleted and when. Meta says it has produced substantial logs from those servers and is still searching backups on a rolling basis, and that there is no basis to allege deletion.

If you build or fine-tune models on third-party content, assume that shell history, torrent client configuration, and the identity of every engineer who ever pulled a corpus are discoverable and will be read aloud. Three things follow. Keep a dataset provenance register that records, per corpus, the source, the acquisition method, the licence or permission relied on, and the approving manager — because the alternative is reconstructing it from.bash_history under court order. Extend litigation holds to personal machines and former employees: the most damaging testimony in this filing came from someone who had left the company three years earlier and deleted a dataset from his own computer. And govern secondary internal uses of any acquired corpus, because under the per-use rule a reading group can forfeit ground that the training defence had already won.

### The dates to hold

From the statement and the discovery orders it describes: amended complaint by 6 November 2026; supplemental interrogatory responses on the schedule Meta agreed (30 October and 6 November 2026); privilege-log disputes to Judge Hixson by 13 November 2026; a further joint discovery letter brief on the remaining interrogatory disputes, or a notice that none remain, by 17 November 2

Meta.content:
# 外媒指稱Meta攜手中國新創傅利葉智能打造人形機器人原型機「Max」：搭載NVIDIA晶片與Muse AI

## 二代機「Max 2」已於9月啟動研發

💡 本文重點摘要

- 核心亮點一：Meta 攜手中國傅利葉智能（Fourier）開發人形機器人「Max」，由副總裁親自駐點上海工廠，利用長三角供應鏈優勢僅耗時 3 個月即完成首台原型機。
- 核心亮點二：硬體規格搭載 NVIDIA Jetson Thor 運算晶片與五指靈巧手，二代機「Max 2」更計畫新增微投影機與爬樓梯感測器，鎖定美式家庭環境的日常家務助理需求。
- 核心亮點三：該計畫旨在將 Meta「Muse AI」與 Llama 模型實體化，儘管官方為避開地緣政治審查聲稱僅供內部研究，但其軟硬體整合進度顯示 Meta 正加速布局消費級機器人市場。

Meta繼去年初在Reality Labs內部成立專屬機器人部門，並且在今年5月收購機器人AI新創Assured Robot Intelligence (ARI)後，私底下的硬體研發進度似乎比外界想像得還要快且大膽！

根據The Information網站獨家調查報導，知情人士揭露Meta Platforms已經攜手中國上海機器人新創「傅利葉智能」 (Fourier，以GR-1 / GR-2人形機器人聞名)共同開發出一款內部代號為「Max」的人形機器人原型機。

更驚人的是，Meta機器人產品副總裁甚至親自飛往中國，在上海工廠駐廠長達近兩個月，讓雙方僅耗時短短3個月就造出第一代「Max」實機，更已經在今年9月火速啟動第二代原型機「Max 2」的研發工作。

## Meta x 傅利葉人形機器人「Max」與「Max 2」關鍵細節

綜合知情人士披露與各大財經外媒轉述的核心內容，Meta這項保密到家的機器人計畫包含以下五大重點：

第一代原型機「Max」規格：高約150公分、搭載NVIDIA Jetson Thor晶片與五指靈巧手

這台內部代號為「Max」的人形機器人原型機，身高接近5英尺 (約1.5公尺)、體重約106磅 (約48公斤)。在硬體與算力配置上：

核心大腦：採用NVIDIA Jetson Thor機器人專用超級運算晶片；

外觀與交互：頭部配備可模擬人類臉部表情的顯示螢幕 (Expressive display)與揚聲器，雙臂末端則配置具備抓取能力的五指靈巧手 (Five-fingered hands)。

## 高管駐點上海工廠兩個月，「中國供應鏈速度」3個月搓出實機

為了以最快速度驗證軟硬體整合，Meta機器人團隊親自飛往中國與傅利葉智能展開貼身協作。其中，Meta機器人產品副總裁Li-Chen Miller更直接在傅利葉位於上海的工廠駐點工作將近兩個月，雙方僅花費短短3個月時間便從零打造出「Max」原型機，並且於今年8月底的Meta內部機器人高峰會 (Internal robotics summit)上正式向部分員工進行實機展示。

### 9月已經啟動二代機「Max 2」研發：新增微投影機、強化爬樓梯與抓握能力

在8月底完成內部展示後，Meta與傅利葉隨即於今年9月展開第二代原型機「Max 2」的開發工作。據悉，「Max 2」將迎來四大硬體升級：

重新設計的軀幹結構 (Redesigned torso)；

改良升級的靈巧手 (Improved hands)，以更精準地抓握與操作居家日常物品；

內建投影機 (Projector)，可在牆面或桌面上直接投射互動介面；

增設更多環境感測器，專門協助機器人在家庭環境中「上下樓梯」 (Navigate stairs)。

### 戰略定位：成為Meta「Muse AI」代理的實體化身，瞄準家務助理

知情人士指出，執行長Mark Zuckerberg與Meta高層將人形機器人視為其核心「Muse AI」模型與代理物理世界的實體延伸 (Physical extension)，長遠目標是開發出能進入一般消費者家庭、協助處理日常家務 (Household tasks)的機器人，並期望未來能在機器人部門端出更成熟的商業化產品 (目前尚未設定具體上市時間表)。

### Meta 官方緊急降溫聲明：「僅供內部研究與實驗，無計畫對外販售」

針對The Information網站的報導，Meta官方隨後向媒體回應表示，目前與傅利葉智能的合作僅聚焦於「內部研究與技術實驗」 (Internal research and experimentation)，公司「沒有計畫對外銷售這些與傅利葉合作生產的機器人產品」 (No plans to sell the units)。

## 為什麼明知華府盯得緊，Meta也要派人前往上海蹲點兩個月找傅利葉打造「Max」？

從產業供應鏈與地緣政治的角度來看，Meta這次找上上海傅利葉智能、花三個月造出「Max」，背後藏著三個非常值得深思的戰略算盤：

### 為什麼不找美國本土新創，偏偏派高管去上海蹲兩個月？

因為「3個月造出整機」只有中國長三角與珠三角供應鏈辦得到！

回顧 2025 年初 Meta 技術長 Andrew Bosworth 成立消費級人形機器人部門時，外界曾盛傳 Meta 接觸過美國本土明星新創 Figure AI ，以及中國的 宇樹科技 (Unitree)。但為什麼最後第一台原型機「Max」是跟上海的傅利葉智能（Fourier）生出來的？

原因非常現實：Meta最強的是軟體與視覺語言動作模型（Llama / Muse AI + 今年 5 月收購的 Assured Robot Intelligence 全身控制演算法），但 Meta 自己沒有做諧波減速機、行星滾柱絲槓、空心杯馬達與高自由度靈巧手的機械工廠！ 如果你在美國矽谷從頭開模訂製一台 150 公分高、48 公斤重、還要改軀幹跟塞投影機的人形機器人，光等零件交期可能就要一年；但 Meta 的產品副總裁 Li-Chen Miller 直接飛去上海傅利葉工廠駐廠兩個月，利用上海周邊極度成熟的機電致動器供應鏈，短短 3 個月就把「Max」一號機造出來，8 月底開完內部展示會，9 月馬上就能改圖紙做「Max 2」！

對急需真實物理關節與靈巧手來收集家庭環境訓練數據（Real-world physical data）的 Meta 來說，用中國硬體的速度來餵養美國 AI 的大腦，是時間成本最低的捷徑。

### 「NVIDIA Jetson Thor ＋ 頭部微投影機 ＋ 爬樓梯感測」：看懂 Meta 對「家用機器人」的產品定義

注意看這次曝光的「Max」與「Max 2」規格細節：

第一，身高刻意控制在 150 公分、48 公斤（106 磅）——這正是為了進入「一般家庭客廳與廚房」最沒有壓迫感、萬一傾倒也不至於壓傷人的黃金尺寸；

第二，大腦沒有硬塞自研晶片，而是直接採用老黃（NVIDIA）專為人形機器人打造的 Jetson Thor 平台，驅動自家的 Muse AI；

第三，「Max 2」居然在機器人身上加了一顆 「投影機（Projector）」 與 「爬樓梯感測器」！想想看，美式獨棟住宅多半有二樓，機器人不會爬樓梯就等於廢了一半；而內建投影機則意味著當「Max 2」走到你書房或廚房時，可以直接把食譜、視訊通話畫面或今天我們剛聊過的《Style Sketch》穿搭建議直接投射在流理台或牆壁上！這完全展現了 Meta 做消費級穿戴裝置（如 Meta Ray-Ban Display）的交互巧思。

### 為什麼 Meta 急著撇清「絕不對外販售這批機器人」？為了閃避華府國會的政治地雷！

最後，為什麼消息一曝光，Meta 公關就立刻向《The Information》強調「與傅利葉合作的機器人純屬內部研究實驗、絕不會拿出來賣」？ 別忘了，現在是 2026 年底，美國政府連中國製的聯網電動車與掃地機器人、無人機都祭出了嚴格的國安審查與進口限制。

如果 Meta 宣布要賣一台「全身裝滿高畫質鏡頭與麥克風、在美國家庭裡到處走動拍隱私、而且是由中國廠商製造」的人形機器人，隔天國會聽證會的傳票絕對馬上寄到Mark Zuckberg桌上！

因此，Meta 的算盤非常清楚 (就如同當年打造 Android 系統或 Quest 頭顯的初期套路)：先借用傅利葉現成且快速的硬體軀幹，在實驗室裡把「Muse AI 機器人大腦與全身控制軟體棧」訓練成熟；等到哪天真的要推出商用量產版家用機器人時，再換上美國本土或台系代工廠來打造合規的量產肉身。

社群社交达人：深度使用Instagram、Facebook或WhatsApp，希望在聊天中即时获取信息或创作内容的社交用户。

跨平台效率追求者：需要同时处理多个文档（如PDF、表格）、快速提取摘要并进行数据对比的职场人士或学生。

# DeepSeek发布全新Agent架构“Super-agent”，让AI调度AI

来源：环球网

【环球网科技综合报道】10月31日晚间，DeepSeek Harness团队在官方公众号发表技术文章《Super-agent设计探索：迈向更自主的Agent系统》，正式公开其面向自主智能体探索的全新架构Super-agent，相关原型已同步开源。

DeepSeek在文中指出，随着模型能力持续提升，AI完成单个任务已越来越不需要人工干预，但人类管理多任务的注意力并未同步增长——一个人通常只能同时跟进3至5个活跃会话，多任务上限正从“模型能力”转向“人的注意力”。Super-agent的核心思路，是将会话管理与上下文同步从人手上移到系统层面，由AI承担调度与执行，人则专注于目标设定与结果验收。

架构上，Super-agent采用Router与Worker双层设计：Router作为持续运行的全局协调节点，统一接收群聊、GitHub、邮件等多渠道消息并分派任务；Worker各自维护独立上下文，并行执行问题复现、代码审查、功能开发等具体工作，必要时可调用Subagent。系统同时引入事件驱动与两级过滤机制，使AI在无人@的情况下也能识别群聊中的潜在缺陷，主动在后台复现并尝试修复。

DeepSeek表示，基于该架构构建的内部Super-agent实例已在日常研发中持续运行，参与问题修复、代码审查响应及Harness自身的迭代。团队同时强调，此次发布系面向工程实践的架构思路探讨，并非对现有产品功能的介绍。（勃潺）

DeepSeek发布全新Agent架构：Super-agent

四川观察

2026-11-01 01:30广东四川广播电视台四川观察官方账号

关注

10月31日晚，DeepSeekHarness团队在官方公众号发表技术文章《Super-agent设计探索：迈向更自主的Agent系统》。

DeepSeek表示，模型能力提升催生了新的应用形态，个人助手（PersonalAgent）开始集中涌现。它们直接接入日常的消息、日程、邮件与工作平台，持续观察信息流并协助处理事务。这种持续在线、事件驱动的工作模式并不局限于个人场景，个人助手只是其中一类应用；在软件开发等商业场景中，它同样很有价值。

然而，现有主流Agent设计还难以在多任务和团队协作的规模上支撑这一模式，多任务上限取决于人的注意力。

Agent的工作模式仍然以单一Session为基本单位，不同Session之间彼此独立。当用户并行推进多项工作时，必须手动切换并记住各个Session的上下文，而据团队观察，一个人通常只能同时跟进3到5个活跃Session。在这种设计下，单任务的上限取决于模型能力，多任务的上限取决于人的注意力。

DeepSeek团队通过双层架构、事件驱动、异步多信道交互、存算分离与外部Watchdog，系统在底层接管了繁琐的会话管理与上下文同步，使人类得以从具体的执行细节进一步上移到更高层的决策与验收。DeepSeek把这种Agent形态及其系统架构称为Super-agent。

文章指出，整套设计并没有提出全新的理论，而是将计算机系统中经典的工程思想应用到了Agent系统的构建中。具体的实现方式会随技术发展而演进，但DeepSeek认为背后的系统设计思路有更长期的参考价值。

目前，DeepSeek基于这套思路和DeepSeek Harness构建的内部Super-agent实例已经在持续运行，日常参与问题复现与修复、代码审查响应与DeepSeek Harness自身的迭代。

当团队成员在群聊中反馈软件问题时，即使没有人主动@AI，它也能识别潜在缺陷，在后台尝试复现问题、寻找修复方案。

值得注意的是，在本篇推文的开始，DeepSeekHarness团队也提示，这是一篇面向工程实践的架构思路探讨，并非对DeepSeekHarness现有产品功能的介绍。

# DeepSeek发布全新Agent架构“Super-agent”，让AI调度AI

来源：环球网

【环球网科技综合报道】10月31日晚间，DeepSeek Harness团队在官方公众号发表技术文章《Super-agent设计探索：迈向更自主的Agent系统》，正式公开其面向自主智能体探索的全新架构Super-agent，相关原型已同步开源。
# Super-agent 设计探索：迈向更自主的 Agent 系统
原创 DeepSeek 产品部 DeepSeek Harness 团队

2026年10月31日 20:29 浙江

6222人

本文是一篇面向工程实践的架构思路探讨，并非对 DeepSeek Harness 现有产品功能的介绍。

## 1. Super-agent

过去一年里，以 Coding Agent 为代表的单任务 Agent 已经证明，模型能够使用工具解决复杂问题，且越来越少需要人类持续监控和逐步干预。与此同时，模型的多 Agent 协同能力也在提升，使跨会话的组织与调度变得可行。随着人类在底层执行中的参与减

DeepSeek在文中指出，随着模型能力持续提升，AI完成单个任务已越来越不需要人工干预，但人类管理多任务的注意力并未同步增长——一个人通常只能同时跟进3至5个活跃会话，多任务上限正从“模型能力”转向“人的注意力”。Super-agent的核心思路，是将会话管理与上下文同步从人手上移到系统层面，由AI承担调度与执行，人则专注于目标设定与结果验收。

架构上，Super-agent采用Router与Worker双层设计：Router作为持续运行的全局协调节点，统一接收群聊、GitHub、邮件等多渠道消息并分派任务；Worker各自维护独立上下文，并行执行问题复现、代码审查、功能开发等具体工作，必要时可调用Subagent。系统同时引入事件驱动与两级过滤机制，使AI在无人@的情况下也能识别群聊中的潜在缺陷，主动在后台复现并尝试修复。

DeepSeek表示，基于该架构构建的内部Super-agent实例已在日常研发中持续运行，参与问题修复、代码审查响应及Harness自身的迭代。团队同时强调，此次发布系面向工程实践的架构思路探讨，并非对现有产品功能的介绍。（勃潺）

DeepSeek has released a prototype autonomous coding agent to take on Anthropic's Claude Code, Bloomberg News reported on Nov. 1.

DeepSeek's Harness team unveiled the open-source agent, called Super-agent, in a WeChat post on Oct. 31, the report said.

Super-agent monitors group chats among developers on its own and gathers views on coding problems. It proposes solutions first even if users do not summon it.

In a user manual posted on GitHub, DeepSeek said its goal is to "minimise what people need to worry about as much as possible and maximise the value gained as much as possible."

DeepSeek formed the Harness team early this year. The team supports the development of AI agents that will compete with coding services from major U.S. AI research and development companies including Anthropic. Harness is software that wraps large language models, enabling AI agents to handle more complex tasks. Developers including Anthropic have also been designing their own harnesses to make work such as coding more efficient.

DeepSeek has also secured funding to compete with Anthropic and OpenAI. It raised about $15 billion in a recent funding round ahead of an initial public offering.

# DeepSeek unveils AI ‘super agent’ in coding race with OpenAI, Anthropic

Technical paper proposes approach that reduces need for humans to coordinate multiple AI agents and monitor their progress

Ben Jiangin Beijing

Chinese artificial intelligence start-up DeepSeek has previewed a plan for a more autonomous AI agent that can handle multiple tasks with minimal human intervention, as it steps up competition with US rivals OpenAI and Anthropic in developing coding assistants.

The proposed system, dubbed super agent, aimed to reduce the need for humans to coordinate multiple AI agents and monitor their progress, addressing a key bottleneck in managing today’s increasingly complex workflows, according to a technical article published by the company’s DeepSeek Harness team on Saturday.

DeepSeek said that advances in AI models had fuelled the emergence of agents that could automate a growing range of tasks, from managing calendars and drafting emails to preparing work reports and writing code.

However, managing multiple agents simultaneously still demanded considerable human attention, the team said.

“Single-task limits depend on model capabilities, while multitask limits depend on human attention,” the paper said.

The DeepSeek team estimated that a person could typically oversee only three to five active AI agent sessions simultaneously, limiting the productivity gains from deploying multiple assistants.

DeepSeek’s proposed system seeks to overcome this by automatically distributing tasks among agents and coordinating their work, leaving humans to focus on decision-making and reviewing results.

The initiative comes as competition intensifies among AI developers to build more autonomous coding assistants, with Anthropic’s Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex increasingly capable of handling complex software development tasks.

DeepSeek’s proposal seeks to take agent automation further by allowing multiple agents to work simultaneously and proactively respond to events such as messages and code updates without requiring explicit instructions for every task.

Under the proposed architecture, a central coordinating agent would distribute assignments among multiple independent agents, which could execute tasks in parallel and report their progress to the central agent, reducing the need for human oversight.

In one example, the team said an agent could detect a software bug reported in a group chat and independently attempt to reproduce and fix it, even without being directly instructed to do so.

If it identified a viable solution, the agent could submit a proposed code change for human review. Otherwise, it would remain silent to avoid unnecessary interruptions, the team said in the paper.

In experimental tests, the approach enabled completion of one task in just under 16 minutes, compared with more than 29 minutes for a conventional approach, according to the team’s findings.

Some industry experts acknowledged that DeepSeek was making progress in the right direction, but questioned whether the proposal offered meaningful advances over existing systems.

“The challenge in AI software development today is ensuring reliability … rather than completing tasks faster,” said Liu Ming, a Beijing-based AI entrepreneur, on China’s Quora-like platform Zhihu.

DeepSeek itself acknowledged potential challenges around security and privacy, including the risk that malicious instructions could compromise the agents connected to other services and systems.

DeepSeek released an open-source research prototype of the super agent on code hosting platform GitHub, while stressing that the initiative remained an architectural exploration rather than a mature product.

Qwen.description: 据公开信息，2026年8月至10月，阿里陆续将Qwen3.8系列的多款模型开源，覆盖旗舰、中型稠密和轻量三档，形成了较为完整的产品梯度。

# 阿里Qwen3.8系列开源：旗舰权重首次开放

发布时间：2026-11-01 00:25 更新时间：2026-11-01 00:25 阅读量：1

在国产大模型的开源节奏里，阿里通义千问的Qwen系列一直是更新频率较高的一个分支。据公开信息，2026年8月至10月，阿里陆续将Qwen3.8系列的多款模型开源，覆盖旗舰、中型稠密和轻量三档，形成了较为完整的产品梯度。

## 三款模型各自解决什么问题

先看旗舰型号Qwen3.8-Max。它采用约2.4万亿参数的稀疏MoE架构，每Token激活约950亿参数，上下文窗口达到1M，并原生支持多模态。对开发者来说更关键的一点是，这是Qwen系列首次开放旗舰级模型的权重，此前这类规模的模型通常只以API形式对外提供。

面向本地部署场景的是Qwen3.8-27B，这是一个稠密模型，采用Apache 2.0许可证。素材显示，做INT4量化后其体积约在14至17GB之间，对单卡或小规模推理环境相对友好，适合有数据不出内网需求的团队做私有化尝试。

最轻的一档是Qwen3.8-Flash，总参数125B、激活仅6B，主打API调用成本。据了解其API价格可低至每百万Token输入1元、输出3元，适合调用量大但对单次推理质量要求不极端的业务。

## 稀疏MoE背后的成本逻辑

把这三款模型放在一起看，会发现一个共同取向：总参数可以做得很大，但每次推理真正激活的部分被压得很低。这正是稀疏MoE架构的价值所在——模型容量与推理开销被拆开处理，训练阶段堆规模，服务阶段控成本。

这一思路在2026年的国产模型中相当普遍。行业分析普遍提到，旗舰模型集体转向稀疏MoE，万亿级参数下激活控制在千亿上下，推理成本随之明显下降。对站长和中小团队而言，这意味着过去只能在实验室里跑的大模型能力，如今有机会以可承受的单价接入线上业务。

如果打算在自有服务器上试跑27B这一档，可以用如下命令先确认显卡与内存条件是否够用，具体阈值以官方模型卡说明为准：
nvidia-smi
free -h
df -h /data
部署环节常见的做法是通过推理框架加载量化权重，把模型目录与端口规划好再启动服务。下面是一段示意性配置，实际参数需按所用框架版本调整：
# 示例：以量化权重启动本地推理服务
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model /data/models/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ \
  --served-model-name qwen3.8-27b \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --port 8000
需要提醒的是，1M上下文的完整能力对显存和框架支持都有较高要求，本地环境通常需要按实际硬件下调上下文长度，具体以官方文档和实际环境为准。

## 开源竞争进入落地阶段

Qwen3.8系列的开源并不是孤立事件。同一时期，智谱、面壁智能、科大讯飞等厂商也在持续放出模型权重，且不少强调国产算力适配与端侧部署。有行业分析把这轮变化概括为从“权重可下载”走向“模型+工具+生态”的体系化竞争。

对建站和运维人群来说，这类开源模型的实际价值在于选择权：既可以用API按量付费快速接入，也可以在自有服务器上做私有部署，把数据留在内网。选哪条路，取决于业务对成本、时延和数据合规的具体要求，建议先在小流量场景验证效果，再决定是否扩大投入。

# 阿里千问接入 Apple 智能：这不是一次普通合作，而是国产大模型第一次站上全球生态的牌桌

你手里的国行 iPhone，终于要「聪明」起来了——而且这次，帮它变聪明的不是苹果自己，是阿里的千问。

10 月 31 日，阿里巴巴官宣与 Apple 达成合作，将千问（Qwen）集成至 Apple 智能（Apple Intelligence）。中国用户可以在 Siri、系统级写作工具以及视觉智能里，直接调用千问的文本与图像理解、内容生成能力。这些功能 11 月 4 日起随 iOS 开发者 Beta 开放测试，12 月随 iOS 27.3 正式上线。

这件事看起来只是「又一家接入了一个模型」，但把它拆开看，会发现它可能是今年国产大模型最值得记住的一步。我不打算堆参数，只想跟你聊四个真正重要的判断。

一、这是国产大模型第一次「进」苹果的牌桌，而不是被「装」进某个 App

过去我们谈国产大模型出海，大多是「我自己做个 App，去海外跟人卷」。但这次不一样——千问是作为系统级能力，嵌进 iOS 的底层体验里。用户不用下载任何新应用，不用切换账号，在 Siri 里说话、在写作工具里打字、在相机里「询问千问」，调用的就是千问。

这意味着什么？意味着千问第一次不是「一个中国产品」，而是「一部全球主流手机在中国市场的默认智能」。这种牌桌位置，比任何应用商店榜单都更值钱。它是入口，不是功能。

二、苹果为什么选千问？因为它要的是「合规 + 本地化 + 够强」的三件套

苹果智能在中国迟迟不上，卡的一直是两点：监管备案，以及中文与本地场景的真正理解。7 月 15 日，网信办公告「Apple 智能」已通过生成式 AI 服务备案；这次合作的落地，说明千问在合规、数据本地化、中文能力上都过了苹果的硬门槛。

更关键的是，苹果要的是一个「懂中国用户说话方式、懂本地生活场景」的模型，而不是把一个英文模型机翻过来凑数。千问在中文理解、图像生成、视觉识别上的积累，正好是苹果最短的那块板。这是一次典型的「各取所需」：苹果拿到合规的中文大脑，阿里拿到全球顶级分发渠道。

三、隐私条款，反而值得普通用户多看一眼

这次有两个细节我特别想划重点。第一，在任何问题、文档、图片发给千问之前，Siri 都会先征得用户同意。第二，用户请求和生成的回复「均不会被阿里巴巴用于模型训练」。

你可以把它理解成一种「托管的智能」：能力借给你用，但你的对话不变成别人的养料。在大家都习惯了「免费换数据」的今天，这条写进官方公告的承诺，其实比功能本身更稀缺。当然，承诺是一回事，落地执行和监管是否到位是另一回事，这一点我们保持关注就好。

四、对普通 iPhone 用户，它到底改变了什么？

说人话：以前你对着国行 Siri 说话，它常常听不懂、答不好；12 月之后，你问它「帮我把这段会议纪要写成邮件」「拍张菜单一看这是什么、热量多少」「用我相册里这张图生成一段朋友圈文案」，背后站着的会是千问。

它不是让你「多装一个 AI App」，而是让原本就每天都在用的手机，突然变得能听懂人话。这种「无感升级」，往往比炫技更能改变习惯。

写在最后：普通人该从中看到什么

我个人的看法是，这件事的象征意义大于功能意义。它说明国产大模型的能力，已经强到能被全球最挑剔的硬件生态当作「底座」来用；也说明「模型之争」正在从「谁参数大」转向「谁能被装进最多人的日常」。

对咱们普通人来说，别急着神话它，也别无视它。等 12 月正式上线，真机用一用，看看它到底帮你省了多少事、又有没有犯傻，才是最实在的。

你用的是国行 iPhone 吗？对于「Siri 背后换成国产大模型」，你是期待多一点，还是担心隐私多一点？评论区聊聊你的真实想法。

# Self-improving AI the key step towards AGI but safety is key: Z.ai founder

Tang says RSI represents a ‘new paradigm’ of R&D that will accelerate AI development even more than it has been

2-MIN READ2-MIN

0

Vincent Chowin Shanghai

Using artificial intelligence to build even smarter systems will make artificial general intelligence (AGI) more achievable, though it would need to be done safely, leading Chinese computer scientist Tang Jie said at an event in Shanghai on Saturday.

The remarks underscore how AI companies in the US and China are both chasing the holy grail of recursive self-improvement (RSI), where increasingly powerful AI systems also become better at improving themselves in an ever-accelerating “loop”.

“[Recursive self-improvement] is the main research problem for [achieving] AGI,” said Tang, who is a computer science professor at Tsinghua University and co-founder of Beijing-based artificial intelligence model company Z.ai, developer of the GLM family of models.

AGI refers to a hypothetical AI system that matches or surpasses human beings in all cognitive tasks.

In recent months, leading US AI start-ups OpenAI and Anthropic have both said that they are starting to see the early signs of RSI. In September, Claude developer Anthropic released a report showing that AI was leading 26 per cent of internal research and development on AI development in August, up from around 1 per cent in March.

Tang did not disclose how much of Z.ai’s R&D was now being done by AI. However, he said in his keynote speech at the World Laureates Forum that RSI represents a “new paradigm” of R&D that would accelerate AI development even more than it has been.

Earlier this year, Tang was one of the first Chinese AI experts and industry leaders to identify RSI as the next stage for AI development.

Last month, Z.ai said that its latest GLM-5.3 model helped optimise its own “inference” infrastructure – the software needed to serve a model quickly and efficiently – for Chinese chips, which had not previously been done before at the same scale.

In his speech on Saturday, Tang said that as frontier AI models shifted from being simple chatbots to AI agents tasked with complex scientific and research projects, it was logical to turn to AI systems themselves for help, given that human researchers were facing greater engineering difficulties as well as financial constraints.

RSI was a major theme of this year’s World Laureates Forum, an annual gathering of leading global scientists, with several Chinese industry and academic experts sharing presentations about how AI was accelerating the design and manufacturing of semiconductors, which are themselves used to power AI systems.

However, some experts have warned that RSI could lead to humans losing control over AI as the development process accelerates too quickly for humans to understand or intervene.

Acknowledging such concerns, Tang called for human researchers to be “humble” in the face of RSI, arguing that the responsibility for ensuring AI progresses safely should be “shared”.

“Probably … the world should organise something together so that we can guarantee the safety for not just one country but for all the world,” he said.

Tang spun Z.ai, also known as Zhipu AI, out of his Tsinghua University laboratory in 2019, with many of his former and current students going on to become core researchers at his company.

Several of his students have become key figures in China’s AI industry in their own right, including Moonshot AI CEO Yang Zhilin.

The most concrete tease is commercial. Wccftech says OpenAI announced that customer token limits will reset on a banked basis, a move the outlet reads as a push to get customers spending on Astra. If that reading is right, OpenAI wants heavy users to burn through allowances now and expect a bigger model soon. It is a familiar tactic in subscription software, where a limit reset ahead of a launch fills the pipeline with fresh usage.

The naming matters too. GPT-6 Astra is the flagship that OpenAI describes as its strongest model overall. A GPT-6.1 Astra would be a point release of that flagship, not a new tier. OpenAI already uses the 6.1 label elsewhere, since GPT-6.1 Terra is exposed in the API under the identifier gpt-6.1-terra. A 6.1 Astra would therefore line up the top model with the newer mid-tier release, and it would suggest OpenAI is on a faster refresh cycle than in previous years.

Nothing here tells us what GPT-6.1 Astra would change. No benchmark, price or context window for a 6.1 model appears in the reporting. Anyone quoting specs for it today is guessing, and we will not add to that pile.

## GPT-6 Astra by the Numbers: The Baseline

Before judging any successor, it helps to pin down the current model. OpenAI’s API identifier is gpt-6-astra. Documentation relayed by LiteLLM lists a context window of 1,050,000 tokens with a 128K output cap and a knowledge cutoff of April 30, 2026. Sources disagree slightly on the launch date, with LiteLLM pointing to September 3 and our earlier coverage citing OpenAI pages that say September 9. We use early September 2026 to stay on the conservative side.

Item | GPT-6 Astra detail | Basis 
---|---|---
API identifier | gpt-6-astra | OpenAI API documentation 
Launch window | Early September 2026 | Sources differ (Sept. 3 vs Sept. 9) 
Context window | 1,050,000 tokens | LiteLLM day-zero notes 
Maximum output | 128K tokens | LiteLLM day-zero notes 
Input price, short context | $10.00 per 1M tokens | OpenAI pricing page 
Output price, short context | $50.00 per 1M tokens | OpenAI pricing page 
FrontierMath Tier 4 | 98% | Vendor-reported 
ARC-AGI-3 | 99.9% | Vendor-reported 
ExploitBench | 100% | Vendor-reported 

Those three benchmark scores come from OpenAI itself, and no independent lab result appeared in the material we reviewed. Our deeper look at the GPT-6 Astra copy claim also notes that OpenAI’s safety overview rates Astra as its first model to reach the Critical level of cybersecurity capability under its Preparedness Framework. That detail raises the stakes of any copying story, because a model with that profile is exactly what a rival would want to imitate.

## The GPT-6.2 Betelgeuse Mystery

Betelgeuse is the part of the story with the least behind it. Wccftech says the name surfaced inside OpenAI’s internal model tracker. The outlet also mentions a base model called Bel with more than 10 trillion parameters, though it does not tie that figure to a published OpenAI document. We treat both details as unverified leaks until OpenAI says otherwise.

A public tracker run by a developer named Benjamin Nieuwenhuijzen shows how thin the trail is. His AI Radar feed flagged the string gpt-6.2 after it appeared in a single news headline, which happened to be the Wccftech piece. The maintainer declined to act, noting that the only source was a third-party headline about a teased or rumored model and that no official OpenAI announcement or release existed under that name. In plain terms, the name has one source, and that source is the article that started the discussion.

That does not make Betelgeuse fake. Labs routinely keep internal codenames that never reach customers, and leaks of those names are common. It does mean readers should not build plans around a GPT-6.2 launch. A sensible reading is that OpenAI has more than one model in testing, and that the hype around the next release now outruns the facts.

Advertisement

Hype has a function here. A leaked codename keeps attention on OpenAI during a week when rivals are shipping and when Anthropic is reportedly preparing a public listing. Whether the leak was deliberate or accidental, it works as free marketing for the lab that wants to look like it is two steps ahead.

## What the Personality Test Found

The distillation evidence in the Wccftech report comes from a personality comparison. According to the outlet, the test draws on personality indexes from Artificial Analysis. It found that Kimi K3.1 Pro behaves like GPT-6 Astra, and that GLM-5.3 behaves like Anthropic’s Claude 5 series. Wccftech concludes that both Chinese models are likely products of distillation, or at least of heavy stylistic influence through synthetic data.

### Kimi K3.1 Pro and the Astra match

The Kimi result lines up with the earlier Reuters report. The Information said Moonshot relied heavily on Astra outputs, and the personality test now shows a model whose conversational habits resemble the teacher it allegedly learned from. Two independent angles pointing the same way carry more weight than either alone, though neither amounts to proof.

### GLM-5.3 and the Claude 5 match

The GLM-5.3 finding is new, and it names a different teacher. Z.ai’s model reportedly reads like a member of the Claude 5 family. The Reuters story did not mention Z.ai at all, so this is the first public suggestion in this news cycle that a third lab, and a second American model, sit inside the story.

### DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 shows no such match

The control case is just as telling. Wccftech says DeepSeek’s V4.1-Flash-1017 showed no similar affinity in the same test. That is awkward for the broader narrative, since Reuters named DeepSeek alongside Moonshot. Either the personality method misses some distillation, or the reporting about DeepSeek rests on something the personality test cannot see. Both explanations are plausible, and the public record does not choose between them.

## Distillation Explained: Evidence Versus Proof

Distillation means training one model on the outputs of a stronger one. The student learns to imitate the teacher’s answers, reasoning traces or tone. Labs use the method on their own models all the time, because it produces smaller and cheaper systems that keep much of the larger model’s quality. The controversy begins when the teacher belongs to a competitor.

A personality match is circumstantial evidence. Models trained on similar internet text, similar human preference data or similar synthetic datasets can drift toward similar voices without any direct copying. A shared habit of hedging, a shared taste for bullet lists or a shared refusal style can show up in two models that never touched each other’s outputs. That is why Wccftech hedges with the phrase heavy stylistic influence, and why we read the test as a signal and not a verdict.

Stronger proof would look different. It would include logged API traffic from accounts tied to a lab, leaked training manifests, or side-by-side tests where one model reproduces another’s quirks on unusual prompts. None of that is public. As of November 1, 2026, OpenAI, DeepSeek and Moonshot had not replied to Reuters in the coverage we reviewed, and we found no on-record statement from Z.ai or Anthropic either.

Whether the alleged practice breaks any vendor’s terms of service is a separate legal question, and no report we saw answers it. Readers should keep the technical question (did this happen?) apart from the legal one (was it prohibited?) and the commercial one (does it matter to buyers?). The three get blurred in headlines, and they deserve different levels of confidence.

智谱AI发布的大语言模型系列

# GLM-4.7系列模型

GLM-4.7模型是智谱AI发布的大语言模型。该模型于2025年12月23日上线并开源，主要面向编程（Coding）场景进行优化，优化内容包括编码能力、长程任务规划与工具协同 [2-3]。2026年1月20日，GLM-4.7-Flash发布并开源，该模型为混合思考模型，总参数量为30B，激活参数量为3B，替代GLM-4.5-Flash [1] [17] [22]。

2025年12月28日，在Artificial Analysis的“AA智能指数”中，GLM-4.7得分为68分，在开源模型中排名第一；在Hugging Face全球趋势榜中排名第一 [7-8]。在百万用户盲测的编程评估平台Code Arena中，GLM-4.7在开源模型和国产模型中的排名均为第一 [4] [14-15]。GLM-4.7发布后，Vercel、Kilo Code、Roo Code、Cline等AI平台宣布接入GLM-4.7 [7-8] [24]。

## 研发背景

智谱自2020年启动GLM预训练架构研发后持续迭代，其统一模型融合推理、编码与智能体能力 [23]。北京市发展改革委支持建设了一批公共算力基础设施，GLM-4.6、4.7等系列均依托北京市公共算力平台完成训练研发 [16]。

## 发展历程

2025年12月23日，智谱AI正式上线并开源新一代旗舰模型GLM-4.7 [2-3] [5] [9-10] [14]。

2025年12月25日，云计算服务商优刻得（UCloud）宣布在其AI算力云服务平台接入GLM-4.7模型 [6]。

2026年1月20日，智谱发布并开源了轻量版混合思考模型GLM-4.7-Flash，该模型总参数量为30B，激活参数量为3B [1] [17] [22]。GLM-4.7-Flash提供了免费调用服务，并替代了上一代GLM-4.5-Flash模型 [1] [17]。上一代免费语言模型GLM-4.5-Flash将于2026年1月30日下线，下线后相关请求将自动路由至GLM-4.7-Flash [17]。

## 产品服务

GLM-4.7主要面向编程（Coding）场景，功能涉及编码能力、长程任务规划与工具协同 [2]。GLM-4.7在编程、推理与智能体三个维度中，涉及多语言编码和在终端智能体中的效果 [15]。GLM-4.7支持交错思考、保留思考和轮次级思考，其中交错思考在每次响应和工具调用前进行思考，保留思考在编程代理场景中自动保留思考块，轮次级思考支持在单次会话中对每一轮推理进行控制 [13]。

在前端生成方面，GLM-4.7可生成网页、PPT、海报；在办公创作中，PPT 16:9适配率由52%变为91% [16]。GLM-4.7的功能涉及聊天、写作与角色扮演等方面 [14]。GLM-4.7-Flash除编程场景外，还可用于中文写作、翻译、长文本、情感/角色扮演等通用场景 [17]。

GLM-4.7提供API服务，并设有Skills模块，支持多模态任务的统一规划与协作执行 [19] [21]。在本地部署方面，GLM-4.7支持包括vLLM和SGLang在内的推理框架 [13]。

## 核心技术

GLM-4.7系列模型的关键技术范围包括思考机制、上下文与部署兼容和轻量化型号 [13] [17] [20]。

### 思考机制

GLM-4.7采用交错思考，模型在每次响应和工具调用前都会进行思考，从而提升指令遵循能力和生成质量。保留思考在编程代理场景中使模型自动在多轮对话中保留所有思考块，复用已有推理结果，而不是从头重新推导，以减少信息丢失和不一致性，适用于长周期、复杂任务。轮次级思考支持在单次会话中对每一轮的推理进行控制，对于轻量级请求可关闭思考以降低延迟/成本，对于复杂任务则启用思考以提高准确性和稳定性 [13]。

### 上下文与部署框架

GLM-4.7支持约200K输入上下文和128K输出上下文 [20] [25]。GLM-4.7兼容vLLM、SGLang等主流推理框架，transformers使用版本4.57.3 [13] [20]。对于GLM-4.7的智能体任务，通过添加配置开启Preserved Thinking模式（仅SGLang支持），enable_thinking为true，clear_thinking为false [13]。

### 轻量化型号

GLM-4.7-Flash是一个混合思考模型，总参数量为30B，激活参数量为3B，可用于轻量化部署 [17] [22]。

### 技术效果与成本

为追求更高的推理质量，模型倾向于生成详尽的思维链，这一策略在提升答案可靠性的同时，也相应增加了推理成本 [12]。

## 运营模式

2025年12月23日，智谱上线并开源GLM-4.7模型。GLM-4.7提供API服务，并支持Skills模块，用于多模态任务的统一规划与协作执行 [19] [21]。

2026年1月20日起，GLM-4.7-Flash替代GLM-4.5-Flash上线 [17] [22]。GLM-4.5-Flash将于2026年1月30日下线，下线后相关请求将自动路由至GLM-4.7-Flash [17]。

GLM-4.6、GLM-4.7发布即适配寒武纪、摩尔线程芯片 [18]。

## 重要事件

2025年12月23日，智谱AI上线并开源GLM-4.7模型 [2-3] [5]。2025年12月28日，在国际评测榜单Artificial Analysis的“AA智能指数”中，GLM-4.7模型综合成绩为68分，位列全球第六，在开源模型和国产模型分类中排名第一 [7-8] [11-12] [23]。该模型在开源社区Hugging Face全球趋势榜排名第一。GLM-4.7发布后，Vercel、Kilo Code、Roo Code、Cline、Factory Droid、Okara、Fireworks等AI平台宣布接入GLM-4.7 [7-8] [24]。2025年12月25日，云计算服务商优刻得（UCloud）宣布在其AI算力云服务平台接入GLM-4.7模型 [6]。2026年1月20日，智谱GLM-4.7-Flash发布并开源 [1]。

## 行业影响

在Artificial Analysis公布的“AA智能指数”中，GLM-4.7得分为68分，排名第六；在开源模型与国产模型分类中均排名第一，得分高于Claude 4.5 Sonnet、Grok 4及DeepSeek V3.2等模型。榜单显示，除GLM-4.7外，Kimi K2 Thinking与DeepSeek V3.2均获67分，以一分之差紧随其后 [12]。

在全球百万用户参与盲测的Code Arena中，GLM-4.7在开源模型和国产模型分类中排名第一，排名高于GPT-5.2 [14-15] [19]。在SWE-bench-Verified测试中，GLM-4.7在开源模型中排名第一，较上一代GLM-4.6提升5.8%；在LiveCodeBench V6评测中得分为84.9分，在开源模型中为SOTA，并高于Claude Sonnet 4.5 [16] [19]。

GLM-4.7发布时适配寒武纪、摩尔线程芯片 [18]。GLM-4.7-Flash在SWE-bench Verified、τ²-Bench等主流基准测试中的综合表现高于gpt-oss-20b、Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507；在相同和近似尺寸模型系列中，其开源模型得分为SOTA [17]。

# 智谱认领神秘模型“牛来”：10万张国产芯片承载每日百万亿 token

- AI
- 0

智谱正式确认，此前在开发者社区引发热议的匿名模型Ox Alpha（中文社区称“牛来”）就是其最新发布的GLM-5.3-Flash。该模型测试期间每日100万亿token的流量，全部由超过10万张国产芯片承载，智谱称其硬件效率与单token成本已达到与主流英伟达GPU相当的水平。

消息公布后，智谱港股盘初一度大涨逾7%，股价报1106港元；半导体研究机构SemiAnalysis评论称，CUDA护城河再度受到考验。

## 匿名测试与流量纪录

GLM-5.3-Flash在正式亮相前以匿名形式在OpenRouter和OpenCode上免费开放测试，代号Ox Alpha，中文社区称其为“牛来”，模型代号灵感来自国内近期热映的同名电影。

智谱披露的数据显示，该模型在5天内累计流量超过50万亿token，刷新了这两个平台的流量增长纪录，当前使用量已超过DeepSeek的两倍以上。

测试期间每日100万亿token的流量规模，此前被认为只有顶级前沿实验室才具备相应的算力支撑，这也是SemiAnalysis在评论中特别提及的一点。

## 10万张国产卡的部署细节

智谱在官方技术文档中说明，该模型的推理服务调用超过10万张国产芯片组成的集群，并称硬件效率及单token成本已达到与主流英伟达GPU相当的水平。

文档描述了这套集群的技术难点：单张芯片的主要瓶颈在于内存容量与带宽，支持长达100万token的上下文长度尤为困难。为此，智谱在SGLang基础上构建了专用推理引擎，采用W8A8量化、INT8/FP8/BF16混合缓存量化以及节点内张量并行等技术。

集群还引入了生产级Encode–Prefill–Decode（EPD）分离式架构，将多模态编码、prompt预填充和逐token解码拆分为可独立调度的工作池。智谱称，与同一硬件上的初始基线相比，端到端服务性能提升了3倍。

据《晚点LatePost》了解，这批芯片的供应商或来自华为、摩尔线程与海光。智谱官方对此未予置评，技术文档中也未明确具体芯片型号。

## 模型参数与定价策略

GLM-5.3-Flash的参数规模为320B总参数、激活参数18B，参数量约为上一代旗舰GLM-5.3的40%，与DeepSeek V4 Flash几乎持平。

定价方面，该模型每百万token输入0.8元、输出2.8元，缓存命中价格0.23元，为GLM-5.3的十分之一，上线前两周实行半价。智谱表示，其定价为GLM-5.3的1/10，限时折扣内为1/20，为Claude Opus 4.8的1/40。

与调价后的DeepSeek V4 Flash相比（谷时输入1.5元、输出4.5元），GLM-5.3-Flash在绝大多数常规调用场景下更便宜。

## 架构调整与性能评测

GLM-5.3-Flash采用了与GLM-5.3完全不同的架构设计。与GLM-4.5相比，其总参数量相近（355B对320B），但激活参数量从32B降至18B，层数从92层减至45层，几乎减半。

智谱称，该模型是首个采用稀疏注意力与线性注意力混合架构的开源前沿模型。相较于GLM-5.3，其注意力计算量与KV缓存大小分别降低了3.01倍和4.44倍。

它也是GLM-5系列首个原生多模态模型，支持图像和视频输入，是智谱战略聚焦coding以来首次推出具备多模态能力的新模型。

智谱官方评测显示，GLM-5.3-Flash在Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index中取得57分，超过上一代旗舰GLM-5.2，与Anthropic的Claude Opus 4.8持平，也高于DeepSeek旗舰模型V4 Pro正式版的53分。

## 涨价潮中的低价切入

GLM-5.3-Flash的发布发生在中国AI模型市场一轮集体涨价之后。Kimi K3输出价格高达每百万token 100元，超过前代K2.6三倍以上；智谱上半年提价后输出价格也达到28元；DeepSeek V4 Pro从6元涨至13.5元，高峰时段27元；DeepSeek V4 Flash输出价格从2元涨至4.5元，高峰时段9元。

《晚点LatePost》指出，涨价的直接后果是需求外溢：DeepSeek V4 Flash提价后，在OpenCode平台上的调用量下滑了一半，这部分需求成为国产模型厂商新的增长空间。GLM-5.3-Flash的定价策略正是瞄准了这一缺口。

市场层面，消息公布后智谱港股盘初一度大涨逾7%，股价报1106港元；MINIMAX-W跟涨6%。半导体研究机构SemiAnalysis在X平台发文称，继OpenAI自研推理芯片Jalapeño宣布之后，CUDA护城河再度受到考验。

## 要点

- Ox Alpha即智谱GLM-5.3-Flash
- 测试期每日流量达100万亿token
- 推理集群使用超10万张国产芯片
- 定价为Claude Opus 4.8的1/40
